points.text: The ecosystem catalyst theme was rejected by the Challenge: price, TVL and volume do not confirm demand, so there is no case to raise WMON above 20%.
The unlock theme was weakened: schedule is real but sell-through is unknown and partly priced in. It argues against raising the target, not for cutting it by 5 points or more.
The current plan already has a 20% target, a 20000 bps volatility brake and a cost hurdle of 40 bps, which suit the thin depth and high vol.

body.whatWouldChangeIt: Evidence of real sell-through ahead of Nov 24, or price, TVL and volume jointly confirming demand, would justify moving the target.

points.text: MON up 5.18% in 24h at $0.02481 after Robinhood listing and privacy news; the bounce sits inside a high-volatility regime (7d realized 115.84879%).
Monad TVL fell 3.2% over 7 days to about $1008M; DEX volume about $52.7M per day, up only 0.8%.
Nov 24 cliff unlock of roughly 16.6B MON, against a market cap of about 293M USD; sell-through unknown and the event is widely known.
Pool and oracle agree closely; a 10000 USD sell costs about 89 bps impact, so depth is thin at size.

body.summary: MON is about $0.0248 after a 5.18% bounce in 24h, but is well below its Oct 1 level. Volatility is very high. Monad TVL is slightly down and DEX volume is flat. A large token unlock is scheduled for Nov 24. The plan sits at a 20% WMON target.
The schedule is real but the sell-through is unknown and the event is widely known, so the downside skew is unproven. Confidence should stay low. The kill criterion is too noisy to be useful.

objections.text: Unlocked is not sold. The thesis admits there is no evidence of recipient selling. The reported $60M investor buyback offer was reportedly declined by nearly everyone, which points to low sell intent.
The event has been public for weeks, so much of it is probably priced in. MON is up 5.17847185% over 24h, and 7d realized vol of 115.84879% swamps any slow supply effect.

The kill criterion is weak. Price must hold above 0.0300 USD, roughly 20% above the current ~$0.0248. With vol this high that level can be crossed by noise, and the foundation extension branch is hard to observe.

The conclusion barely binds the account. The plan is already at 20% WMON, with the target range capped at 30%, a vol brake of 20000 bps, and 40% as the hard max. A 10000 USD sell costs ~89 bps, so a hold is the default.
Sources disagree on size (16.6B to 17.1B) and on whether investors release one tranche or twelve, and they are mostly one news origin.

Realized volatility is high (7d 115.84879222904864), so a 24h bounce carries little signal.
A reported 16.6B token unlock on Nov 24 is a larger supply overhang than these announcements are likely to offset.
Sentiment posts say Monad under-delivered versus hype; attention only, not proof.

notes.title: ACTIVATION Scan: MON recent catalysts and Nov unlock risk
notes.notes:
Market snapshot shows orderly conditions. MON up 5.18% in 24h on Oct 6-7 catalysts: privacy announcement (18% jump), Robinhood listing, Category Labs Private Settlement, StraitsX stablecoins announced. Price now at $0.02481, oracle-pool deviation only 0.257 bps (tight). 

TVL down 3.2% over 7d ($1008.4M, from $1.04B peak Sept 19), but within normal range and no incident signals. DEX volume stable at $52.7M daily (+0.8%). Volatility 81.56% 24h, 115.85% 7d (moderate-elevated, normal for stage).

Two themes identified: (1) MON_UNLOCK_NOV24 — major cliff vesting Nov 24 releases 16.6B tokens (33.6% of market cap), 46 days out, publicly known but not yet fully priced, creates medium-term downside risk. (2) MON_ECOSYSTEM_CATALYST — recent privacy/enterprise/listing announcements are positive story drivers; need to assess if they lead to meaningful on-chain activity that can absorb or exceed the Nov unlock supply.

No evidence of manipulation or distress. This is a normal multi-catalyst trading environment. Depth is strong for the account's position size. Yields on USDC are available (1.25% to 10.8% depending on protocol).

Data gaps: None identified. All major metrics present and current.
